title: CoTr: Efficiently Bridging CNN and Transformer for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
layout_note: Inverted U laid across three side-by-side dashed panels: the CNN-encoder rises from the input slice at the bottom left, the multi-scale features cross the DeTrans-encoder panel left to right along the top, and the decoder descends to the output slice at the bottom right. The detail inset fills the lower half of the middle panel under the layer stack.
grouping: Three dashed black rounded panels of equal height, each titled in large plain sans at the top (CNN-encoder, DeTrans-encoder, Decoder), divide the figure by stage. Block type is carried by fill: grey for CNN blocks in the outer panels, yellow for transformer layers in the middle. Curly braces gather the three flattened feature columns into the layer stack and split them out again. The Deformable Transformer Layer inset is a yellow-filled rounded box with a bold title, set under the layer stack inside the middle panel.
shapes_depth: Flat square-cornered grey rectangles with thin outlines and no shadows, stacked as a pyramid that narrows upward in the encoder and widens downward in the decoder, so box width stands in for resolution. DeTrans Layers are tall yellow rounded rectangles with their label rotated 90 degrees, followed by an ellipsis. Flattened features are thin vertical bars with a white-to-grey gradient. In the inset, MS-DMSA is a stack of offset salmon-to-brown cards, Layer Norm boxes are pale green, Feed Forward is saturated blue, and 'Reference point' is a stack of blue cards. Operators are small circles lettered F (flatten), R (reshape) or +. The CT slices for input and output and a stack of noise images for the positional encoding are drawn as tilted parallelograms in perspective.
proposed_highlight: The proposed DeTrans-encoder is the centre panel, the widest of the three, and its yellow layers are the only coloured blocks against the grey CNN blocks on both sides; one layer is expanded into a yellow detail inset tied to it by two thin grey zoom lines, inside which the proposed attention (MS-DMSA) is the largest and most layered box. The Flatten and Reshape steps that bridge CNN and transformer are tagged with green-outlined speech-bubble callouts at the panel borders.
lesson: Conversion steps between the two model families (Flatten, Reshape) are tiny lettered circles on the arrows, each named once by a speech-bubble tag, so the interface is visible without adding boxes to the pipeline.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2103.03024); venue MICCAI recorded from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar). The caption serves as the colour key (grey = CNN blocks, yellow = deformable Transformer layers); the drawing has no legend and no tensor-size labels, and 'Upsampling' is the only arrow label in the overview. Filed as u-shape because the data path arches (up the encoder, across, down the decoder) although the panels read as a left-to-right pipeline. The CT slices and positional-encoding images are embedded rasters and are left out of the measured palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: three dashed-outline panels left to right, CNN-encoder -> DeTrans-encoder -> Decoder, with multi-scale CNN features flattened, merged by braces into a row of yellow DeTrans Layer columns, then split and reshaped into the decoder

relations.form: CT volume at bottom-left -> a stack of grey CNN feature bars -> flatten (F) and add positional encoding -> yellow DeTrans layers -> reshape (R) -> grey decoder bars -> segmented CT volume at bottom-right
thin lines open from one DeTrans Layer down into a yellow inset 'Deformable Transformer Layer' (MS-DMSA stack, Layer Norm, Feed Forward, Layer Norm, with blue reference points)

three feature scales each pass an F node and a ⊕ where vertical lines from the noise-textured positional-encoding sheets enter from below; braces then gather the three token bars into the transformer and fan them out again
input and output are tilted CT slices, the output overlaid with coloured organ masks

channels.colour: yellow = the deformable transformer contribution (layers and inset); grey = CNN feature maps and decoder features; light green = callout outlines naming operations (Flatten, Reshape, Positional encoding) and also the Layer Norm boxes; inside the inset orange = MS-DMSA, bright blue = feed forward and reference points; organ colours on the output
channels.shape: grey bars = feature maps, thin vertical bars = flattened token sequences, tall yellow columns = transformer layers, lettered circles = flatten/reshape, ⊕ = addition, speech bubbles = operation names
channels.line: solid arrows for all flow; curly braces merge and split the token sequences
channels.frame: dashed rounded frames = the three network parts; a solid yellow frame = the zoomed layer

quality.strengths: The new part (the deformable transformer) is the only saturated region and is opened once in an inset tied to one layer; real CT input and a coloured segmentation output bracket the flow; multi-scale tokens are drawn as separate bars entering and leaving the transformer.
quality.weaknesses: CNN and decoder blocks are unlabelled grey bars, so resolutions and stages are left to the caption; light green marks both callout bubbles and Layer Norm boxes; three operations are named in speech bubbles stuck onto the lines; the positional-encoding lines rise a long way through the panel to their ⊕ nodes.

insights.structure: Three dashed-outline panels left to right (CNN-encoder, DeTrans-encoder, Decoder); the middle panel holds a row of yellow vertical 'DeTrans Layer' boxes and an inset yellow box zooming into one 'Deformable Transformer Layer'.
insights.data: Input and output are tilted CT slices (output overlaid with coloured organ masks); multiscale features are grey bars; positional encodings are a stack of noise-textured sheets; flattened tokens are thin vertical grey bars.
insights.emphasis: Yellow fill marks the transformer contribution and the zoomed inset shows its internals (MS-DMSA stacked boxes, layer norm, feed forward, reference points); green speech-bubble callouts name 'Flatten', 'Reshape', 'Positional encoding'.
insights.flow: Up the CNN encoder, rightwards through flatten (F) and add nodes into the transformer, out via reshape (R) and down the decoder to the segmented slice at bottom-right; curly braces gather the multi-scale tokens.
insights.avoid: The positional-encoding sheets and several lines cross the panel border, and the callout bubbles add visual noise for simple ops.

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded panels with titles at top, plus a solid yellow zoom inset inside the middle panel
arrangement.inputs_as: a tilted real CT slice at the bottom of the left panel
